label: Dee's Reformed Table — Post-1587 Revision
description: After the 1587 disruption, Dee received instructions to reform the Great Table — a revised version with specific letter changes. The relationship between the original and the reform is itself debated. Not all scholars agree on which changes belong to the reform and which are scribal corrections.

dateRange.notes: Post-disruption period; exact date of reform uncertain

provenance: Dee received instructions — attributed to the angel Raphael — to reform the Great Table after the traumatic disruption of 1587. The reformed version exists in Dee's later manuscript entries in Sloane 3191 and related manuscripts. It is sometimes called the Tabula Recensa.

modifications.description: Specific letters were changed in the reformed version. The exact count and nature of changes is debated among scholars. Peterson identifies a set of changes; Leitch identifies a partially overlapping but different set.
modifications.attributedTo: John Dee (attributed to angelic instruction via Raphael)
modifications.reason: Reform instructions received during the post-1587 angelic sessions

elementalQuarters.label: Quadrant NW — same structural arrangement as original
elementalQuarters.notes: The reform changed individual letters, not the structural arrangement of quarters.

stateData._dataStatus: TRANSCRIBED — Uses the Reformed/Tabula Recensa letter arrangement, which is the same grid adopted by the Golden Dawn. The reform changed individual letters from the 1584 original but maintained the same structural layout. Cells marked 'probable' because the exact scope of Dee's reforms is debated (Peterson and Leitch reconstruct different change sets). Cross-check against Tyson p.167 and Peterson's digital editions recommended.
